A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DCTdiff and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-C. Retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation, with no essential evidence gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, FID comparisons, training-convergence measurements, compression and upsampling results, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds 512×512 generation, model-scaling experiments, inference timing, additional quality metrics, and block-size ablations.

M1.justification: The DCTdiff pipeline, frequency tokenization and pruning, entropy-consistent scaling, frequency-reweighted objective, SNR-scaling procedure, and inverse-DCT generation remain unchanged. The revisions alter parameter settings and experimental configurations without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 adds FFHQ 512×512 and AFHQ 512×512 generation and extends reconstruction-compression evaluation to FFHQ 512×512. This introduces higher-resolution generation requirements and an animal-image domain beyond the retained datasets. ImageNet 256 reconstruction examples already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: Pixel UViT, latent UViT, DiT, and the existing compression/upsampling comparators are retained. Latent UViT was already evaluated in v1 Table 3. The rows incorrectly labeled UViT in v1's DiT Table 5 become DiT in v2 Table 4, consistent with the original caption, surrounding text, and unchanged baseline scores.

E3.justification: Reported settings change substantially: scaling percentile τ becomes 98.25 rather than 96.5, several SNR factors change, and FFHQ 256 DCTdiff training steps increase from 200k to 300k. New protocols vary model depth and size, evaluate IS/precision/recall/CMMD, and time 10k generated samples on one A100. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish the provenance of every revised result.

E4.justification: v2 adds model-capacity analyses on three datasets, a B=4 versus B=8 block-size ablation, and inference-time versus quality analyses. Appendix B also revises the coefficient-pruning controls: ECS variants with m=0, 7, and 8 precede frequency reweighting, replacing the earlier m=0, 8, and 9 study. The c=3 SNR ablation is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability around benchmark scores. The existing 50,000-sample Monte Carlo procedures in Appendices A.1 and A.4 remain unchanged; additional metrics do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Many DCTdiff scores are revised alongside changed settings, including FFHQ 256 DPM-Solver FID at NFE=100 from 5.92 to 5.08. Newly reported NFE=100 results are 7.07 versus latent UViT's 10.89 on FFHQ 512 and 8.76 versus 10.86 on AFHQ 512. v2 also adds timing, scaling, additional-metric and ablation results, and revises reconstruction scores, including FFHQ 256 m=8 from 0.58 to 0.49.

T1.justification: v2 removes Section 4.3's assertion that reconstruction FID determines a lower bound on generative FID. Theorems 5.1 and 5.2, their appendix proofs, and the SNR derivations otherwise retain their mathematical substance. Renaming reconstruction FID to rFID does not change its calculation.

C1.justification: The abstract explicitly claims 512×512 generation and superiority to SD-VAE latent diffusion at one-quarter training cost. The introduction's contributions and conclusion extend the claimed advantage from pixel diffusion to latent diffusion. v1 instead described its FFHQ 256 latent comparison as competitive.

C2.justification: New discussion explains the balance between VAE overhead and DCTdiff's additional Transformer tokens, qualifies inference efficiency by sampling steps and generation quality, and identifies a block-size tradeoff between convergence speed and quality. These extend the interpretation locally; the spectral-autoregression explanation and limitations concerning 1024×1024 generation and frequency-specific architectures remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.6 adds 512×512 configurations, SD-VAE parameter counts, and parameter-selection guidance; the timing experiment specifies its A100 hardware and sample count. Code access is unchanged. Conversely, Appendix C.1 removes the explicit 16× VAE compression ratio for the unchanged reconstruction comparison. The new guidance also says τ=98 while the main text and tables specify 98.25.

R1.justification: Sections 2.2 and 5.3 add discussion of wavelet diffusion, DCT-based VampPrior, spectral tokenization, and recent frequency-autoregressive work, including Phung, Kuzina and Tomczak, Esteves, Yu, and Huang. Some attention/linear-layer references are removed, and dataset/metric citations are added. These refine the existing positioning without replacing its central distinction between frequency modules and full DCT-space modeling.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites portions of related work and the scaling explanation, separates cost and scalability into Sections 6.3-6.4, adds Appendices A.7-A.9 and an Impact Statement, and reorders ablation and qualitative subsections. Authorship and affiliations also change. The main narrative structure and most method and proof prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds a front-page AFHQ image panel, expands and replaces generated-sample grids, restructures the high-resolution and training-cost tables, and adds timing, scaling, metric and block-size displays. The earlier ablation tables are reorganized into Table 14. Existing pipeline, theoretical, compression and upsampling figures are largely retained or relocated, rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the scalability and efficiency case, which v1 supported mainly with experiments up to 256×256 and convergence iterations. The 512×512 human/animal comparisons, computational and wall-clock measurements, complementary metrics, and capacity/block-size analyses address important validation gaps. The broader latent-superiority claim still needs qualification: latent UViT wins most FFHQ 256 comparisons, and DCTdiff is slower at high NFEs. Those overstatements and small reporting defects, including the omitted VAE compression ratio, temper but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support and diagnostic detail.
